Marcus / Sabrina — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary up front:

- For UK-resident patient data, in most cases a UK Addendum (IDTA) is required in addition to SCCs unless the TIA includes specific UK-prescribed safeguards and your legal team accepts them. Redwood's standard hosted offering has a UK Addendum template we can propose, but we can also scope a TIA addendum that maps to the same controls.

- We will provide a current subprocessor map and a short matrix showing which subprocessors have access to pseudonymized vs. identifiable fields. Short answer: no external subprocessor should receive cleartext patient identifiers for the pilot — we use prefix/KV caching and in-flight encryption for identifier tokens, and downstream analytics are run on pseudonymized payloads. I'll attach the subprocessor CSV and a draft TIA scoping doc.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to send the subprocessor map + short access matrix today.
2) Jonas to prepare a TIA draft that includes a UK Addendum option (two-track approach) — target EOW (Fri).
3) We set a 30-minute call on Tuesday for legal teams to align on whether Aurelian accepts the TIA-based UK safeguards or wants the formal IDTA.

If that works I'll route attachments and links.

Thanks,

Hi Sabrina / Marcus — following up with the TIA scoping decision tree we discussed on the call this morning. Core points: 

1) Two-track approach (recommended):
   - Track A: UK Addendum / IDTA executed (standard legal route). Best for regulated studies where explicit UK-prescribed safeguards are required by compliance teams.
   - Track B: TIA + Redwood-prescribed UK safeguards (operational controls + binding TIA language). Faster DPA amendment route and typically acceptable for pilots where data residency and technical measures are explicit in scope.

2) Proposed pilot default: Track B with option to escalate to Track A before production. Rationale: reduces time-to-start while preserving the option for a formal IDTA.

3) Implementation items and timelines (we've added these in the Drive doc):
   - Redwood to deliver redline-ready TIA + optional UK Addendum by Fri 21 May.
   - Aurelian legal to review and return comments within 5 business days.
   - Subprocessor attestation (Laura): subcontractor access confirmed within 48 hours; telemetry export disabled for pilot unless explicitly enabled.

4) Evidence package we will hand off: SCC implementation checklist (controls matrix), TLS/KMS configuration docs, subprocessor SOC2 summaries (where available). If you need certified copies (SOC reports), we can coordinate with our Security team via an NDA channel.

If Aurelian wants the IDTA route, we can start parallel paperwork but expect an extra 2–3 weeks to finalize signatures. Please confirm which track you want to proceed with and whether procurement needs a pricing amendment for the KMS/backup option.

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call if helpful.

Jonas Weber
